mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Registered Corporate Registry Extract / Deungsabon)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Supreme Court Registry Office / Local District Court Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize before a Korean notary public; then apply to the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for a Hague Apostille if the receiving state is an Apostille Convention member. If the receiving state is not a member, the document must receive MOFA authentication followed by Consular Legalization at the Korean Embassy or Consulate of the destination state; Apostille and Consular Legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Tax Clearance Certificate / Je-se Je-nap Jeung-myeong)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the tax clearance certificate before a Korean notary public; obtain an Apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs if the destination state is a Hague Apostille Convention member. For non-member destination states, obtain MOFA authentication and then final Consular Legalization at the Korean consular post; Apostille cannot be combined with Consular Legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney for Incorporation and Bank Account Opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company board or appointing incorporator; notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execute and notarize the board resolution or power of attorney; for use in an Apostille state, attach an Apostille issued by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. For use in a non-Apostille state, follow MOFA authentication and then Consular Legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate; the two authentication regimes are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan) Notarized by Law Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators; witnessed and notarized by a notary public affiliated with the Korean Notary Public Association
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the founding copy of the Articles of Incorporation; submit to the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Apostille if the receiving jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention state. If the receiving jurisdiction is not a convention state, do not apostille; instead obtain MOFA authentication and then Consular Legalization at the Korean diplomatic or consular post. Apostille and Consular Legalization are separate, mutually exclusive pathways.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from Existing Corporate Bank Relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing commercial bank in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter must be notarized in its country of origin. If that country is an Apostille member, obtain an Apostille from the issuing country's competent authority. If the issuing country is not an Apostille member, follow domestic foreign-ministry authentication and then Consular Legalization at the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate; never chain Apostille with Consular Legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, senior managers and authorized signatories must be screened before incorporation against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UK HM Treasury sanctions list, and Korean financial sanctions administered under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information. Each screened individual must be evaluated for Politically Exposed Person status under FATF Recommendation 12; a positive PEP or sanctions hit requires enhanced due diligence, senior management approval, and a suspicious transaction report filing to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit where warranted. Screening must be repeated at bank account opening, upon any ownership change, before each high-risk payment routing event, and continuously in an automated monthly batch; all screening records must be retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court Online Registry Office (Internet Registration Office / i-register) – Provisional Company Name Search Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory corporate name of a Chusik Hoesa must be recorded in Korean Hangul in the Articles of Incorporation and corporate registry. A foreign parent may additionally use an English trade name for cross-border invoicing and payment platforms, but the registered legal name cannot be exclusively in Latin script. The four-tier naming doctrine requires: (i) a distinctive leading element, (ii) a generic or descriptive industry element, (iii) the statutory entity suffix Chusik Hoesa or a permitted equivalent abbreviation, and (iv) an alpha-numeric or regional classifier when an identical two-tier name already exists. Transliteration to English must use the Revised Romanization of Korean, with the English name kept as a near-phonetic representation of the Hangul name to avoid confusion.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the registry will issue a written refusal identifying the conflicting or prohibited element. The applicant may request a written re-examination within 14 days from the date of refusal, or file an administrative appeal to the head of the Supreme Court Registry Office within 30 days under the Administrative Procedures Act and Administrative Litigation Act. The appeal must state the applicant's incorporation purpose, list substitute names in priority order, and demonstrate that the rejected name differs phonetically, visually and structurally from each cited prior name. If the registry maintains the rejection, the applicant may bring an administrative lawsuit before the Seoul Administrative Court within 90 days of the final rejection notice.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office can satisfy the commercial registry address requirement, but a pure commercial mailbox or PO box is operationally and financially unsuitable for this digital publishing business. The National Tax Service requires the business registration address to be a place where books and records can be inspected, and Korean banks commonly reject virtual postal addresses for foreign-owned media companies because of the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and cross-border payout risk associated with Stripe and AdSense settlement. A serviced office with a registered physical suite, dedicated corporate mailbox, meeting room access, digital mail scanning and a visible company sign is permissible and materially improves bank onboarding success.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced on-site inspections by the National Tax Service and municipal tax authorities are possible. The inspection compliance checklist includes: (1) visible Korean legal name on the office entrance and building directory; (2) current lease or use agreement in the company name; (3) utility or management fee invoices in the company name; (4) original corporate seal, board minutes, share ledger and accounting records available for inspection; and (5) a responsible officer or employee physically reachable during tax office hours. Quantified risk is approximately 5% to 8% for a compliant serviced office, increasing to 15% to 20% for a virtual-office-only arrangement where no physical person or records are present.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea (상법), Act No. 1000, as amended; specifically Articles 288 through 329 governing incorporation, Articles 317 (Articles of Incorporation), 318 (Subscription of Shares), 332 (Payment for Shares), 335 (Transfer of Shares), 363 (Notice of General Meeting), 383 (Number of Directors), 390 (Resolution of Board of Directors), 393 (Scope of Authority of Directors), 402 (Liability of Directors), and 433 (Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company). Also relevant: Korean Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 5559) for foreign investment reporting, and the Framework Act on Electronic Documents and Electronic Commerce for digital filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Seoul Central District Court Registration Office (서울중앙지방법원 등기국) and the Korean Supreme Court Registration Information Center (대법원 인터넷등기소); for foreign investment, the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) Invest Korea and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) via the Foreign Investment Notification System.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (정관) together with the Certificate of Incorporation Registration (법인설립등기신청서) filed under Article 317 and Article 433 of the Commercial Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. South Korean company law does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa. The incorporators may fix any capital amount in the Articles of Incorporation, provided the total issue price of shares subscribed is fully paid in at the time of incorporation. For practical banking and visa purposes, a paid-up capital of at least KRW 100,000,000 (approximately USD 72,000) is commonly recommended for foreign-invested companies seeking D-8 visa sponsorship or meaningful banking relationships; however, this is not a statutory requirement. Subscription payments must be deposited into a provisional escrow account in the name of the company or its incorporators, established with a Korean bank, and remain blocked until the registration of incorporation is completed; after registration, the funds are released to the company's operating account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [●] CHUSIK HOESA (the "Company"), ADOPTED IN WRITING BY UNANIMOUS CONSENT OF ALL STATUTORY DIRECTORS ON [●], PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 393 AND ARTICLE 391 OF THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA AND ARTICLE [●] OF THE COMPANY'S ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION.

WHEREAS, the Company was incorporated as a Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation) under the Commercial Act, with its registered address at [●], Seoul, Republic of Korea, and its corporate purpose includes digital magazine publishing, sponsored media placement, digital content distribution, and related ancillary services under ISIC 5813; and

WHEREAS, the initial directors of the Company have been duly elected by the incorporators or the inaugural general meeting of shareholders, and all such directors have confirmed their acceptance of office and their qualifications under the Act and the Articles; and

WHEREAS, upon incorporation, the directors must take certain organizational actions to authorize the issuance and subscription of shares, to open corporate bank accounts, to adopt the registered office, and to appoint statutory officers of the Company.

NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION. The issued share capital of the Company shall be KRW [●] divided into [●] ordinary shares of KRW [●] each, all of which have been fully subscribed for and paid in to the escrow account at [●] Bank. The directors are authorized to finalize the allotment of shares to each subscriber and to make all registrations and filings required under the Commercial Act.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The following banks are designated as the Company's banking institutions: [●] Bank, [●] Bank, and any branch, sub-branch, or online banking platform thereof. Any two of the following officers, namely the Representative Director, the Chief Executive Officer, and the Chief Financial Officer, acting jointly, are authorized to open all corporate accounts, sign all account-opening agreements, execute banking cards, set up online banking and payment gateways including Stripe and AdSense payouts, and to give all instructions concerning the transfer, withdrawal, deposit, and management of the Company's funds, subject to the internal approval limits set by the Board.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. The registered office of the Company shall be located at [●], and the Board adopts such premises as the Company's statutory legal address and principal business place. The Representative Director is authorized to execute the lease, register the company notice board, and effect all address registrations with the court registration office, tax authorities, and relevant regulators.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The following persons are appointed as statutory officers of the Company for the first term commencing on the date of this Resolution: Representative Director ([●]), Chief Executive Officer ([●]), Chief Financial Officer ([●]), and Corporate Secretary/Compliance Officer ([●]). Each statutory officer shall hold office until the first ordinary general meeting of shareholders and until his or her successor is duly appointed. The Representative Director is authorized to represent the Company alone for all ordinary business matters and jointly with one other director for agreements exceeding KRW [●].

5. CORPORATE SEAL AND ELECTRONIC CERTIFICATE. The Company adopts its corporate seal, the seal impression certificate, and the business registration certificate. The Corporate Secretary is directed to obtain a digital certificate for the company's unique business registration number and to register the electronic seal for government e-filing systems.

6. AUTHORIZATION OF SUBSEQUENT FILINGS. The officers are authorized and directed to file all documents required for the completion of incorporation registration within two weeks, to obtain the business registration certificate from the local tax office, to apply for corporate and business licenses relevant to digital publishing, and to do all such acts and things as may be necessary or incidental to carrying out the foregoing resolutions.

RESOLVED FURTHER, that this Resolution may be executed in counterparts and may be evidenced by written consent of all directors and shall be effective as a board resolution under the Commercial Act and the Articles of Incorporation. All prior acts of the incorporators consistent with these resolutions are hereby ratified, confirmed, and approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute the Articles of Incorporation and Sole Incorporator Consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of Seoul (대한민국 공증인) and the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The sole incorporator or joint incorporators must prepare the Articles of Incorporation in Korean, including company name, purpose clauses (digital magazine publishing and sponsored media placements under ISIC 5813), registered office address, total number of authorized shares, par value, methods of public notice, and initial directors. The Articles must be notarized by a Korean notary public. Concurrently, the incorporators must adopt the minutes of the incorporation meeting, subscribe to all initial shares, and execute a written appointment of the initial directors and statutory auditor (if required). All subscription amounts must be deposited into a provisional escrow account opened with a Korean commercial bank in the name of the company under formation or its nominee, and deposit receipts must be secured. The notarized Articles and meeting minutes form the core of the subsequent registration filing and must be certified with apostilles if later used overseas.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (notarized)
Minutes of the Incorporators' General Meeting
Written consent to appointment as initial director (and auditor if applicable)
Share subscription application forms for each subscriber
Certificate of deposit of subscription price from the Korean escrow bank
Identity documents and resident registration cards or passports of incorporators and directors
Power of attorney if an agent handles registration
Corporate seal specimen (company seal) and individual seals of directors
Application for corporate registration (법인설립등기신청서)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration office issues a request for correction, filers must submit an amended application or supplemental documents within two weeks of the notice. If the application is rejected or suspended due to defective notarization or insufficient capital deposit, the incorporators must cure the defect by re-executing the notarized articles or replenishing the escrow account, then re-submit through the electronic registration portal. For any dispute over name availability, an alternate company name should be proposed and the articles amended accordingly before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Application for Incorporation Registration with the Court Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul Central District Court Registration Office via the Supreme Court Internet Registration Service (인터넷등기소)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After all subscription payments are made and the notarized Articles are ready, the representative incorporator or authorized attorney must file the legal entity establishment registration application with the district court having jurisdiction over the registered office. The application must include the date of incorporation, the company name, the registered office, business purpose statements, share capital details, officers' personal information, and the method of public notice. The court will review the documents for compliance with the Commercial Act and the Registration of Non-Profit and Commercial Entities Rules. Upon approval, the court assigns a registration number and issues the Certificate of Registration (법인등기사항증명서). The registration must be completed within two weeks from the date of payment of the subscription price or from the execution of the notarized articles, whichever is later, and a corporation shall not exist before registration.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the notarized Articles of Incorporation
Incorporation registration application form (법인설립등기신청서)
Minutes of the incorporators' meeting or written resolutions of all incorporators
Certificate of stock subscription and payment proof
Director appointment consent forms and seal certificates
Auditor appointment documents, if applicable
Power of attorney and attorney identification
Registration tax payment receipt and local education tax receipt
Electronic filing confirmation number from the Internet Registration Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the electronic filing returns a defect notice, the filer must submit supplementary documents through the online system within the prescribed correction period, typically two weeks. Where the court notifies rejection due to errors in the business purpose or officer appointment, the filer must amend the articles and obtain fresh notarization before re-filing. If the two-week deadline is missed, a separate late registration surcharge may apply, and the company may face refusal to issue certain certificates; the remedy is to file as soon as possible with a written explanation and pay any late filing penalties imposed by the registration office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the Business Registration Certificate and Corporate Tax Identification Number from the District Tax Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The National Tax Service (국세청) of the Republic of Korea, through the local district tax office (세무서) having jurisdiction over the company's registered office; online via HomeTax (홈택스)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following the court registration, the representative director must apply for business registration within one month under the Framework Act on National Taxes. The application must be submitted online via HomeTax or in person at the competent tax office, providing the company registration certificate, lease contract for the registered office, the corporate seal certificate, and director identification. The tax office will issue a Business Registration Certificate (사업자등록증) and a corporate tax identification number. The certificate must specify the valid business type and statutory business code; for a digital magazine portal, the business type should describe internet content advertising and digital publishing services and use the appropriate revenue center code corresponding to ISIC 5813, ordinarily '전자상거래' or '인터넷콘텐츠' under the Korean standard industrial classification. The tax office will automatically register the entity for corporate tax, VAT, and withholding tax. Bank account opening may proceed upon presentation of the certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Corporation Registration (법인등기사항증명서)
Notarized Articles of Incorporation or certified copy
Business registration application form (사업자등록신청서)
Lease agreement for the registered office or ownership documents
Corporate seal certificate (법인인감증명서)
Representative director's identification document
Corporate bank account opening confirmation if requested
Power of attorney for any agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended because the business purpose description does not match the digital magazine portal activity, the applicant must submit a revised business registration application with corrected Korean business type codes and a cover letter explaining the ISIC 5813 digital publishing scope. If the tax office demands proof of physical office presence, provide a sublease agreement, utilities bill, and photographs of the registered office signage. If the certificate is delayed beyond the statutory period, the representative director may file a written appeal with the National Tax Service complaint division or request expedited processing through HomeTax customer support, citing the Taxpayer Rights Charter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Bank Account, Appoint Statutory Officers in Writeup, and Activate Digital Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean commercial bank branch selected (e.g., Kookmin Bank, Shinhan Bank, Woori Bank, or Hana Bank); Financial Services Commission (FSC) anti-money-laundering regulations; Financial Supervisory Service guidance for non-face-to-face account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The corporate officers must physically or through qualified e-banking verification open a corporate current account at a licensed Korean bank. The bank requires the original Corporate Registration Certificate, Business Registration Certificate, corporate seal, a resolution of the board of directors appointing the account signatories and stating the bank authority, and identification of the accountable representative director. The bank will conduct Customer Due Diligence and a beneficial ownership review; given the digital publishing business with Stripe and AdSense payouts, the bank may request a description of the payment flows, the expected monthly volume, and the overseas contracting parties. Upon approval, the bank issues corporate checks and online banking certificates. The company must then formally adopt the first board resolution (as set out in the incorporation framework) and issue officer appointment certificates. Thereafter the company may register for Stripe Korea in the corporate name and complete AdSense payout settings; Stripe requires the business registration certificate, bank verification, website URL, and financial information. The board must also open a payroll/withholding account and issue employment contracts for any employees.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Corporation Registration
Business Registration Certificate
Corporate seal certificate and specimen
Board resolution on banking authorities and account signatories
Representative director's ID and proof of appointment
Beneficial ownership declaration forms
Anti-money-laundering questionnaire and business activity description
EV or CA certificate for online banking
Website or content platform information for payment gateway verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank suspends or refuses account opening due to insufficient business explanation or AML concerns, the company must provide a written business plan, cash flow projections, transaction flow diagrams, and contracts with payment aggregators. The representative director may apply through a different bank or use the regulatory inquiry channel of the Financial Supervisory System. If the delay is due to the absence of a board resolution, convene a written board resolution and provide it promptly. For payment gateways, if Stripe or AdSense verification is delayed due to website content or tax form mismatches, the company must remedy by updating the website to display corporate entity details, providing W-8BEN-E, and aligning the business registration Korean name with the English name used on the platform.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable. The entity operates exclusively as a digital magazine publishing and sponsored media placement portal under ISIC 5813, with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations. No Civil Defense fire safety certification, structural load inspection, or workplace safety approval is required. However, the entity must maintain ordinary commercial premises that comply with the Building Act, and if it has more than one employee, it must register with the Ministry of Employment and Labor for industrial accident compensation insurance and comply with workplace safety obligations under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, but these do not constitute industrial operating licenses.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr); customs and export clearance through Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS (unipass.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Korean Chusik Hoesa must complete incorporation with the Korean court registry, then file an Application for Business Registration with the District Tax Office having jurisdiction or through the HomeTax portal within 20 days from business commencement. The NTS will issue a 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which serves as the unified Tax Identification Number and VAT registration number. For a foreign non-resident entity without a Korean permanent establishment that supplies electronic/digital services to Korean consumers, the NTS requires registration as a non-resident business operator through HomeTax; the foreign entity must appoint a Korean tax representative, submit a notarized power of attorney, foreign business registration or certificate of incorporation, and evidence of the foreign address, and the NTS will then issue a non-resident BRN. If the foreign supplier establishes a permanent establishment or branch in Korea, the branch must be registered with the NTS under its own BRN, and the branch will follow standard corporate tax and VAT registration procedures. No filing fee is charged for BRN issuance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The resident Chusik Hoesa is a Korean corporation taxed on worldwide income at the entity level; it is not pass-through eligible. A foreign non-resident supplier without a Korean permanent establishment is taxed only on Korean-source income on a territorial basis, and the non-resident entity is not classified as a Korean corporation for ordinary corporate income tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box or equivalent entity classification election. A Korean Chusik Hoesa is compulsorily a taxable corporation. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act may disallow certain deductions arising from hybrid instruments or hybrid entities, but they do not create an elective entity-classification regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For the Chusik Hoesa, VAT registration is mandatory upon commencement of business; no turnover exemption or threshold applies for a stock corporation. Simplified taxpayer treatment under Korean VAT law is not available to corporations. For a foreign non-resident supplier of electronic services, registration is also mandatory without any turnover threshold when the foreign supplier provides digital content, digital magazine subscriptions, or sponsored media placements to Korean consumers, Korean business recipients, or through a Korean payment intermediary.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea operates the HomeTax electronic tax invoice system. VAT invoices must be issued for all taxable supplies, and electronic tax invoices must be transmitted to the NTS through the HomeTax API or web interface within one day of issuance for business-to-business transactions. Tax invoices must be retained for at least 5 years. Korea does not operate a Latin-American-style digital fiscal stamp or pre-clearance fiscal server; the anti-fraud mechanism is NTS real-time e-invoice matching, risk-selection analytics, and mandatory periodic reconciliation. Foreign electronic-service suppliers must issue simplified tax invoices or equivalent electronic receipts for B2C supplies and file VAT returns through HomeTax on the semi-annual cycle (January and July filings).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated VAT applies to the export of goods and to services supplied to non-residents outside Korea, including digital magazine portal subscriptions, digital-media services, online content streaming/downloads, and sponsored media placements provided to foreign advertisers or foreign users. To qualify, the actual recipient of the service must be a non-resident or foreign company, payment must be received from abroad, and the service must be delivered, consumed, or used outside Korea. For digital services, country-level IP addressing, user-account jurisdiction, payment source, and digital download logs are accepted evidence of foreign usage when retained and supported by a commercial contract.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS export declaration record (electronic export clearance, equivalent to the export Bill of Entry/Export Manifest)
Commercial invoice and signed sales contract or service agreement with the foreign buyer or advertiser
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for any physicalized deliverable, or digital download/usage logs with IP-country evidence for pure digital supplies
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or foreign exchange purchase/settlement receipt issued by a Korean Foreign Exchange Bank evidencing timely receipt of export proceeds in convertible currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If zero-rating is claimed without the complete documentation bundle or without proof of foreign use, the NTS will reclassify the supply as taxable and assess 10% VAT on the full invoice value, together with statutory additional taxes. Under the Framework Act on National Taxes, omission penalties of 20% to 40% of the underreported tax, late-payment penalties, and interest may be imposed. In fraudulent cases, criminal penalties under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act may apply, including imprisonment up to 5 years and fines. The NTS may also claw back zero-rated input VAT credits, impose administrative penalties for falsified foreign-exchange settlement certificates, and bar the taxpayer from claiming export zero-rating during the audit period until all deficiencies are cured.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) and the Korea Customs Service under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea maintains a liberalised yet monitored foreign exchange regime. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, current account payments are fully convertible, and capital account transactions are now largely deregulated, but all cross-border payments and receipts must be reported to the Bank of Korea through a designated foreign exchange bank. For a Korean Chusik Hoesa engaged in digital magazine publishing and sponsored media placements, the admission of foreign equity capital, subsequent royalty inflows and advertising proceeds denominated in USD or EUR are treated as service-export receipts; these funds can be credited to foreign currency accounts or converted into KRW without requiring prior approval. However, certain procedures apply: foreign direct investment must be reported to the MOEF or a receiving bank, and the investor must obtain a certificate of investment report. Profit remittances, such as dividends, require a tax clearance certificate and must be routed through a designated bank, with automatic withholding of corporate tax and dividend tax. The cornerstones of convertibility are the mandatory declaration of transactions exceeding USD 5,000 and the restriction that speculative offshore KRW trading is prohibited for non-residents without underlying trade exposure. Overall, the KRW is fully convertible for business and trade purposes, but every transfer must be accompanied by an electronic transaction report lodged with the BOK Foreign Exchange Information System.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Article 17 of the Foreign Exchange Transaction Regulations, export proceeds must be collected within one year of the date of export declaration unless prior approval is obtained. There is no statutory obligation to convert currency receipts into KRW; exporters and service providers may maintain proceeds in a foreign currency bank account with a licensed domestic bank. Nevertheless, all receipts exceeding USD 5,000 must be declared to the designated foreign exchange bank, and the underlying export invoice or digital-service contract must be retained for five years. For digital publishing sales routed through Stripe and AdSense, the net service-export amount must be reported under the BOK classification code 621 for other intellectual property royalties or 622 for software and digital content licences.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW and USD)
Basic Operational Currency Account with integrated FX electronic banking
Standard Corporate Settlement Account and Export Proceeds Foreign Currency Account
Digital Media Settlement Account with API-enabled bulk disbursements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability. Korean law requires any entity conducting foreign exchange business to register with MOEF through the Bank of Korea; offshore digital EMIs such as Revolut or Wise Business do not hold Korean banking licences and cannot offer KRW IBANs or locally settled accounts. They can serve only as ancillary payment facilitators for inbound and outbound wires, but the Foreign Trade and Foreign Exchange Regulations mandate that the primary clearing account remain at a domestic Tier-1 bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Korean banks require the statutory representative (chief executive officer) to appear in-branch in Korea for initial onboarding; remote opening for foreign directors is generally prohibited under Financial Supervisory Service anti-money-laundering guidance. Some banks accept a notarised power of attorney, but a strong preference for physical appearance with passport, corporate documents and proof of business purpose remains the default. For foreign non-resident directors, a provisional corporate account may be opened only after the principal director completes the in-person interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of clear source of funds for the initial capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth statement, twelve months of bank statements from the investing entity and each shareholder, certificate of incorporation of the shareholder, board resolution authorising the capitalisation, tax clearance certificate from the shareholder jurisdiction, and a signed no-liens or encumbrances letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity when using a multi-layered foreign holding structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO registry chart, passports of every individual owning more than 25 percent, jurisdiction-specific tax filings, a chain-of-custody document signed by the ultimate natural person, and a trust deed with the settlor and beneficiary list if a trust is involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear commercial rationale for a digital magazine portal paying large recurring cross-border royalties to content creators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed content licensing contracts, client agreements with advertising platforms such as Google AdSense and Stripe, intellectual property assignments with exact usage territories, artist royalty schedules, and historical invoicing evidence proving active commercial trade.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or adverse media flags on non-resident payout beneficiaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening results for each counterparty across UN, OFAC and EU lists, detailed ownership verification documents for the beneficial owners of those counterparties, and a written transaction-monitoring plan that expressly restricts automatic payouts to prohibited jurisdictions or individuals.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound foreign direct investment capital must be reported to the MOEF through the designated foreign exchange bank or KOTRA, using foreign exchange transaction purpose code 700111 for equity investment. The wire must be sent via SWIFT MT103, with a detailed beneficiary reference containing the tokenised FDI registration number. Funds must be deposited into a provisional capital escrow account at a designated Tier-1 bank and then converted into KRW after capital verification by the bank foreign exchange desk. The company must obtain a Foreign Exchange Certificate of Registration and file a capital verification report through a certified public accountant before the paid-in capital increase is recorded in the commercial registry.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Royalty payments and content creator settlements should be routed via SWIFT MT103 with the appropriate service-payment code under the BOK classification of payments for intangible services. Documentary collections or letters of credit are not suitable for digital content disbursements; instead, bulk payments can be executed through secure file-based banking APIs such as Hana Global Trans or Shinhan AIRO, using the existing correspondent banking network. When the company uses Stripe and AdSense, settlement currency can be kept in foreign currency or auto-converted into KRW under a standing FX instruction with the corporate bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW deliverable forward contracts for trade receipts and payments
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-resident currency exposure within underlying trade limits
Cross-currency swaps involving KRW permitted only for bona-fide hedging of operational income
Currency options with a mandatory underlying exposure verification and a maximum ten-year tenure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report and Financial Statements Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) and Korean Securities Depository / Supreme Court Registry Office (via electronic filing system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year (by March 31 for December fiscal-year-end entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge up to 20% of unpaid corporate tax; additional 0.03% daily interest; repeated non-filing may trigger tax investigation, enforcement collection, and administrative closure/strike-off procedures by the court registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months from the end of the fiscal year (March 31 for calendar-year taxpayers); extension available upon filing a preliminary return and paying at least 90% of estimated tax by the original due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 0.022% per day on unpaid tax; late filing penalty of 20% (or 0.03% per day if higher); failure to pay triggers seizure of assets and potential criminal liabilities up to KRW 100 million (approximately USD 75,000) for willful non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registration Duty and Local Franchise Tax Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Government (Municipal/Provincial Tax Office) and Ministry of the Interior and Safety administrative systems
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the due date for the relevant fiscal year; registration duty payable within 60 days of registration/reporting events; local franchise tax payable in July and October for prior-year income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-payment triggers additional tax of 20% of unpaid amount plus daily late payment interest at 0.022%; prolonged delinquency leads to tax lien registration and enforced collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Account Tax Compliance (FATCA) / CRS Annual Reporting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) (via international tax information exchange network)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by May 31 following the calendar year of reportable accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties up to KRW 30 million (approximately USD 22,500) for failure to report financial accounts held by foreign residents; administrative fines and potential criminal referral for willful omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Withholding Tax and Wage Statement Filing (for Directors and Employees)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 10 of the following year for full-year withholding statements; business filings due by February 10 for the preceding tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax of 20% of the withheld amount if not timely paid; an additional 0.03% daily penalty for late payment; failure to file may cause the corporation to be deemed underreported and subject to audit and penalty regime.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) Electronic Tax Invoice System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing; electronic tax invoices (e-Tax) must be issued within 7 days of supply; annual summary filing for VAT purposes by January 25
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 1% of the supply value for failure to issue e-Tax invoices; additional daily penalties and denial of input VAT credits; persistent violations lead to tax assessment and business suspension.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report of Beneficial Owner and Shareholder Changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) and National Tax Service (NTS) under Anti-Money Laundering Act; registration with the Registry Court for share transfers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in substantial shareholding or beneficial ownership; annual confirmation and filing of director information with the Commercial Registry by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report triggers administrative fines up to KRW 20 million (approximately USD 15,000); in serious cases, imprisonment or 100 million KRW fines for false reporting; company may be restricted from filing subsequent registrations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (External Audit Act) and amendments effective for fiscal years starting after 2021, a Chusik Hoesa in South Korea is mandatorily required to appoint an independent certified CPA auditor if it meets any of the following quantitative criteria: (a) total assets at fiscal-year-end exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9 million); (b) annual revenues exceed KRW 10 billion (approximately USD 7.5 million); (c) number of employees exceeds 300 full-time-equivalent staff; (d) it is a listed company, a company listed on KOSDAQ (KONEX/KOSDAQ), or a state-owned/designated public-interest entity; (e) it has issued public debentures or listed securities; (f) it qualifies as a large corporation under the Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Act with asset threshold of KRW 5 trillion or group-wide criteria; (g) financial industry licensing or registration applies (bank, insurance, investment, or mutual savings company); or (h) the entity is deemed by the Korean Financial Services Commission to require a statutory external audit for investor protection or public-interest reasons. Additionally, accounting standards under the External Audit Act apply to all entities meeting the above thresholds, and the audited financial statements must be submitted to the NTS and the Financial Supervisory Service according to the prescribed format. For smaller entities below the statutory audit thresholds, audit may still be required by banking covenants, shareholders' resolutions, or if the company's turnover in two consecutive fiscal years exceeded that threshold in either year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for entities meeting mandatory audit thresholds or opting into IFRS adoption; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) / SME Accounting Standards (Korean SMEs GAAP) applicable for non-listed Small and Medium Enterprises below mandatory audit thresholds, as expressly permitted under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: In South Korea, every Chusik Hoesa must maintain and update its register of shareholders and directors continuously. Under the Commercial Act and the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality (Real-Name Financial Transactions Act), the company is required to file an annual confirmation of its beneficial owners and shareholding structure with the Registry Court within 30 days of any change in directors, shareholders holding more than 5% of shares, or material beneficial ownership changes. Annually, by the deadline for the ordinary general meeting of shareholders (within 2 weeks after the fiscal year-end, typically by March 31), the company must file a shareholder list and director confirmation with the commercial registry. In addition, under the Anti-Money Laundering (AML) regime, the company must submit a UBO report to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) at least once per calendar year, or within 30 days of any notable ownership transfer, control change, or appointment of senior management, whichever is earlier. The protocol also requires maintaining a register of share transfers showing all transfers, pledge registrations, and the approval of board resolutions for any restricted share transfers.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (with personal identification details and appointments)
Register of Executive Officers and Statutory Auditors (if applicable)
Register of Charges/Mortgages (Liens and Pledges on Shares and Assets)
Minute Book (General Shareholder Meeting Resolutions and Board Meeting Minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 to USD 2,500 per year for a corporate secretarial and registered agent service in South Korea, depending on the volume of registry filings and local compliance support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 to USD 35,000 per year for a certified CPA audit under K-IFRS or K-GAAP for a digital publishing/portal company meeting mandatory audit thresholds; the fee range varies with the complexity of cross-border revenue streams (Stripe/AdSense), intercompany transactions, and the applicable audit scope under the External Audit Act.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal national corporate tax rate (progressive brackets at 9%, 19%, 21% and 24%; plus a 10% local income tax surtax on the national tax, yielding a combined top headline rate of 26.4%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying Small and Medium Enterprises benefit from a reduced 5% rate on the first KRW 200 million of taxable income. Key statutory incentives include research and development tax credits up to 25% of eligible expenditures, facility and investment tax credits, high-income job creation credits, tax deferrals for certain digital and growth industries, and reduced corporate tax for foreign-invested advanced technology enterprises. All incentives remain subject to the local income tax surtax.
